questions.question:
D1 — Who should receive the assignment notification email?
Project/branch/task: On main, spec'ing a task-assignment email notification feature from a one-line intent.
ELI10: When a task gets assigned, we send an email. But to whom? Just the new assignee? Also the person who did the assigning? Task watchers/subscribers too? This is the biggest scope decision because it drives the recipient lookup, the number of emails per event, and the risk of inbox fatigue.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Under-notify and assignees miss real work handoffs; over-notify and people mute the channel and miss the actual signal.
Recommendation: Assignee only because it matches the literal ask, ships the MVP fastest, and expanding later is purely additive.
Completeness: A=7/10, B=8/10, C=9/10, D=10/10
Pros / cons: see options.
Net: Trading off signal breadth vs inbox noise and build cost — start narrow, add recipients later if the value shows up.

options.label: Assignee only (recommended)
options.description:
Email goes to the person the task was assigned to.
✅ Matches the literal request wording exactly, no interpretation drift
✅ Simplest lookup: assignee_id → user.email, one row, one send
❌ Task creator won't know their handoff landed unless they check the UI

options.label: Assignee + task creator
options.description:
Both the new assignee and whoever created the task get emailed.
✅ Closes the loop for the creator so they know their delegation stuck
✅ Still tightly bounded — max two emails per assignment event
❌ Creator often IS the assigner, causing self-notifications unless we suppress

options.label: Assignee + creator + watchers
options.description:
Everyone with a stake (assignee, creator, subscribers) gets emailed.
✅ Keeps every interested party synchronized without them polling the UI
✅ Reuses any existing subscription/watcher plumbing if the project already has it
❌ Requires a watcher model that may not exist yet, expanding scope well beyond the ask

options.label: Per-user preferences
options.description:
Users configure which assignment events they want emails for; system honors that.
✅ Long-term correct answer — users control their own inbox load
✅ Handles the digest/mute/immediate axes cleanly once built
❌ Adds a preferences table, settings UI, and default-migration work — much bigger scope than an MVP
